summary: The core is built as a scan-time hardware pipeline: H/V-counter-driven map and tile fetches, a per-line sprite scan into ping-pong line buffers fed by a BUSRQ/BUSAK DMA, and a colour mixer that looks up layer priority in the board's priority PROM for each pixel. MAME instead draws whole tilemaps, does a per-frame sprite loop and hardcodes priority through a priority bitmap. None of MAME's decomposition (tile_info callbacks, draw_sprites, the _1943_drawgfx priority hack, the indirect palette build) shows up in the HDL. The only MAME-like piece is an optional HLE security lookup table that is compiled only under a define. By default the build uses an 8751 MCU model.

findings.signal: Priority PROM looked up per pixel
findings.note: Each pixel's opaque bits for char, obj and scr1 plus obj bits 7:6 form the address into bm4.12c, and the selbus output drives the layer mux. MAME hardcodes the layer order and uses a priority bitmap with BMPROM.07 bit 3 instead.

findings.signal: Palette PROMs as RGB lookup, not MAME's indirect-pen tables
findings.note: Per-layer lookup PROMs (hi/lo pairs) sit inside each layer generator, and the final 8-bit pixel indexes the three RGB PROMs directly. MAME instead precomputes resistor-weighted colours and pen-indirect tables.

findings.signal: Map address from H/V counters and scroll adders
findings.note: The H counter is adjusted with flip XORs (HF, H7, SCHF bit construction), added to hpos, and the map ROM address is latched at a fixed SH phase (adv). This is scan-time counter logic, not a tile_index callback.

findings.signal: Tile pixel shift registers stepped by the pixel clock
findings.note: The ROM address is set on HS[2:0]==1, then four plane shift registers shift left or right depending on hflip, one step per 6 MHz cen. This is how a board serialiser works, not gfx-decode.

findings.signal: Sprite DMA by Z80 bus request during VBLANK
findings.note: OKOUT triggers bus_req to the Z80's BUSRQ. A counter (blen/blcnten) then muxes the CPU RAM address and copies the sprites into a buffer. MAME just uses a buffered_spriteram device.

findings.signal: Per-line sprite search into line buffers
findings.note: On each line the engine scans the object RAM, finds Y matches with an adder (Vsum/MATCH), keeps up to 32 objects in a ping-pong buffer, then draws them into a line buffer. MAME instead loops over every sprite per frame with clipping.

Chip selects are decoded from A[15:13]/A[12:11]/A[2:0] like 74LS138 outputs (CSCD, D0CS, D8CS). Control bits are latched from strobes, and flip/sound-reset polarity goes through the M54532 inversion. The register map itself is shared with MAME and is neutral.

findings.signal: Interrupt and wait-state logic from raster bits
findings.note: The IRQ comes from an edge of LVBL && V[7:5]!=3, and wait_n inserts a lost cycle per M1 cycle (mem_wait_n). MAME does not model the CPU slow-down; it uses a scanline-based irq.

A case table maps the protection bytes the CPU writes to the replies it expects. That is a software-style HLE rather than a model of the chip. It is compiled only under JT1943_MCU_HLE; the default build instantiates jttrojan_mcu, an 8751 with real port wiring.

findings.signal: Memory map and register bits match MAME
findings.note: Bank bits 4:2, flip bit 6, char-enable bit 7 and layer enables in bits 6:4 match MAME. Any correct implementation must have these.
